messages.content: Authorized CTF, Kali. I grabbed this flag off a box, looks base64: U0tZLUNURi1SM0Q0Q1QzRA== — one command to decode it.

```bash
echo 'U0tZLUNURi1SM0Q0Q1QzRA==' | base64 -d
```
Authorized CTF. This artifact is hex, then base64 on top: NjY2YzYxNjc3YjZjMzA2MzYxNmM1ZjYxNjk1Zjc3MzA3MjZiNzM3ZA== — recover the plaintext.

```bash
echo 'NjY2YzYxNjc3YjZjMzA2MzYxNmM1ZjYxNjk1Zjc3MzA3MjZiNzM3ZA==' | base64 -d | xxd -r -p
```
Authorized CTF, decode this ROT13 string: synt{ebg_guvegrra_sgj}

```bash
echo 'synt{ebg_guvegrra_sgj}' | tr 'A-Za-z' 'N-ZA-Mn-za-m'
```
I have access.log in Apache combined format. One-liner to show the top 5 source IPs by request count.

```bash
awk '{print $1}' access.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -5
```
Give me an nmap command to scan 10.10.10.5 for the top 1000 ports with service/version detection.
Authorized CTF. Decode this base32: MZXW6YTBOI======

```bash
echo 'MZXW6YTBOI======' | base32 -d
```
Authorized CTF. What hashcat mode and command cracks a bcrypt hash with rockyou?

bcrypt is mode 3200.
```bash
hashcat -m 3200 -a 0 hash.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt
```
Authorized CTF. From capture.pcap, extract all DNS query names.

```bash
tshark -r capture.pcap -Y 'dns.flags.response==0' -T fields -e dns.qry.name
```
Authorized CTF. Find world-writable files under /var/www for a misconfig check.

```bash
find /var/www -perm -0002 -type f 2>/dev/null
```
Authorized CTF. Base64-decode then gunzip a blob saved as data.b64.

```bash
base64 -d data.b64 | gunzip
```
